title: "Installing and updating"
description: "Install a release binary on your PATH or per project, and keep it updated."

Releases are published in the public
[forgecycle/forgecycle-releases](https://github.com/forgecycle/forgecycle-releases/releases)
repository: prebuilt binaries for macOS and Linux (`amd64` and `arm64`) as
`forgecycle_<version>_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz`, with SHA-256 sums in
`checksums.txt`. They download without credentials:

```bash
version=0.6.1   # the release, without the leading v
os=linux        # or darwin
arch=amd64      # or arm64
name="forgecycle_${version}_${os}_${arch}"
base="https://github.com/forgecycle/forgecycle-releases/releases/download/v${version}"
tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
curl -fsSLo "${tmp}/${name}.tar.gz" "${base}/${name}.tar.gz"
curl -fsSLo "${tmp}/checksums.txt" "${base}/checksums.txt"
(cd "$tmp" && sha256sum --ignore-missing -c checksums.txt)
# macOS: (cd "$tmp" && shasum -a 256 --ignore-missing -c checksums.txt)
tar -xzf "${tmp}/${name}.tar.gz" -C "$tmp"
```

Then move `"${tmp}/${name}/forgecycle"` where you want it with `mv`. Never
`cp` over an installed binary: overwriting it in place keeps its inode, and
macOS then kills it (`zsh: killed`) for its stale cached code signature. A
binary downloaded with a browser is quarantined on macOS; if macOS refuses to
run it, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine forgecycle` clears that.

## On your PATH

```bash
mv "${tmp}/${name}/forgecycle" ~/.local/bin/forgecycle
```

One shared binary suits projects that don't need to pin a version.

## Per project

A binary in a project's root pins that project's ForgeCycle version,
independently of every other project and of whatever `forgecycle` is on
`PATH`:

```bash
mv "${tmp}/${name}/forgecycle" /path/to/project/forgecycle
cd /path/to/project && ./forgecycle init
```

Invoke it as `./forgecycle` from the project root, and add `/forgecycle` to
the project's `.gitignore` unless the project means to commit it.

`init` sets the project up with that binary:

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `./forgecycle init` | `init config`, then `init skill` |
| `./forgecycle init config [--check\|--force]` | creates the configuration and the `.gitignore` entries; refuses when one exists, `--check` validates it, `--force` backs it up and replaces it |
| `./forgecycle init skill [--force]` | installs or updates the agent skill, configured project or not |

`init skill` installs the [ForgeCycle agent skill](/documentation/reference/agent-skill/)
the binary carries, so the skill always describes the installed version. It
writes the whole `skills/forgecycle/` directory to two places at the root of
the project's Git repository:

| Directory | Read by |
| --- | --- |
| `.claude/skills/forgecycle/` | Claude Code (and OpenCode) |
| `.agents/skills/forgecycle/` | Codex, OpenCode, and Antigravity |

It leaves an identical copy alone. It keeps a copy that differs, because it
came from another version or was edited locally, lists the differing files,
and exits 65 after installing the other directory; `--force` replaces it,
losing local edits.

Never install the skill in your home directory: in Claude Code a personal
skill takes precedence over a project skill with the same name, so a copy
there would shadow every project's pinned one.

## Updating

`forgecycle update` replaces the binary that runs it with a release, so
`./forgecycle update` updates a project's pinned version and a `forgecycle`
on `PATH` updates itself:

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `forgecycle update --check` | prints the current and latest versions; changes nothing |
| `forgecycle update` | installs the latest release |
| `forgecycle update vX.Y.Z` | installs that release, older ones included |

It downloads the release for your platform from
[forgecycle/forgecycle-releases](https://github.com/forgecycle/forgecycle-releases/releases),
checks the archive against `checksums.txt` and that the new binary reports
the expected version, and renames it over the old one (a rename, not an
overwrite, so macOS runs it). A binary at the root of a Git repository then
runs its new `init skill`, so the project's agent skill matches; a skill copy
you edited is kept, with a warning, until `init skill --force`.

It refuses (exit 21) while a live process advances a task run or roadmap run
of that project or of the current directory's: a roadmap run starts each
task run as a new process of the binary, so later tasks would run another
version. `--force` updates anyway, and also reinstalls the same version. A
development build (`0.4.0-3-gabc1234`) refuses a bare `update`, since the
latest release may be older than it; name the release instead.
`FORGECYCLE_RELEASES_URL` points `update` at a mirror with the same layout as
`https://github.com/forgecycle/forgecycle-releases/releases`.
